# ML-DSA-65 depth 1 sweep: pre-registered predictions (generated by ml_dsa_d1_sweep_predict.py before the measurement)

Model transition (first response size, resolution 100 B): IPv6 23000, IPv4 23400 (difference 400 B).

| hypothesis | IPv6 t6 (B) | IPv4 t4 (B) | t4 - t6 |
|---|---|---|---|
| model as it is (D=0) | 23000 | 23400 | 400 |
| H1 with D=1200 B | 21800 | 22200 | 400 |
| H1 with D=2400 B | 20600 | 21000 | 400 |

Criteria (scored by analyze_mldsa_sweep.py on the sweep, per machine):
- S1 a transition (excess +20 to +35 ms against the cell 200 B below) exists below 22 500 B for IPv6: H1 predicted, a failure to find one rejects any byte undercount.
- S2 t4 - t6 = 400 B within +-200 B (header effect, independent of D): met supports a byte undercount; t4 - t6 close to 0 points to another mechanism (record count, write pattern).
- S3 t6 within 400 B of 20 600 B (= model - 2 400 B, the G3b undercount): met supports that G3b and this have the same cause; a different t6 gives an undercount D = model t6 - measured t6 of its own.
- The sweep says nothing about ECDSA cells (they agree with the model).
